batches.risk: Revokes direct client attachment mutations and cascading parent DELETE/TRUNCATE privileges while retaining SELECT and trusted server grants. Requires integrated Core and legacy Web retention guards. The non-concurrent tenant/document index requires hosted size and lock-impact preflight; both migrations use 5-second lock and 60-second statement timeouts.
batches.recovery: Require backup/PITR and Storage recovery evidence plus isolated restore and migration rehearsal before hosted application. Roll forward or disable attachment submission while retaining privilege denials and the supporting index; never automatically restore unsafe grants. Existing rows, foreign keys and audit history are unchanged. Privileged database-owner and approved tenant-lifecycle operations remain an administrative boundary.

The invoker guard requires active actor and tenant authority, canonical manage/override capabilities and attribution, and makes started evidence immutable. Existing unstamped Web actions are incompatible: pause mobilization writes and release the compatible Web actions and migration as one release unit. batches.risk: Replaces the existing SECURITY DEFINER child trigger function so INSERT, DELETE and ordinary updates continue to recompute their affected DUPA, while an UPDATE that moves a child between DUPAs recomputes both source and destination parents in deterministic UUID-text order. This corrects stale source-parent totals and reduces opposite-move lock inversion, but hosted execution depends on the WO-06 recomputation functions and child triggers being present and can lock both affected DUPA rows. No table shape, stored rows, foreign keys or audit history change; local verification does not establish hosted state or lock behavior.
batches.recovery: Require database backup/PITR, isolated restore and migration rehearsal, and exact-target lock/grant preflight before hosted application. The function replacement is transactional and aborts without data changes on failure. After commit retain the corrected function or roll forward; an emergency restoration of the prior function from 20260812180000_wo_06_dupa_engine.sql reintroduces the stale-source-parent defect and must be a reviewed recovery action. Preserve the existing execute denial for public, anon and authenticated and the service_role grant. This source-only batch does not authorize hosted application.

batches.risk: Adds deterministic advisory-lock and balance guards to inventory reversal paths so a reversal cannot drive stock quantity or value negative under concurrent writes. Existing rows, foreign keys and audit history are unchanged; the migration changes transactional validation and can reject previously unsafe reversals. Local verification does not establish hosted lock behavior or recovery readiness.
batches.recovery: Require database backup/PITR, isolated restore and migration rehearsal, and exact-target lock/grant preflight before hosted application. Roll forward with the guarded reversal path; any emergency restoration of the prior function must be a reviewed recovery action because it reintroduces the negative-balance defect. This source-only batch does not authorize hosted application.
